Designstöd Samarbete mellan Skatteverket - Armeniska Statliga Skattekommittén

description.narrative: Designstöd för att ta fram ett gemensamt projektförslag mellan Svenska Skattemyndigheten och Armeniska Statliga Skattekommittén.

Designsupport for development of a project document and increase the understanding of the Armenian context and a possible cooperation in the near future between The Swedish Tax Authority and The Armenian State Revenue Committee.

The STA will conduct two fact-finding missions on location in Armenia and invite Armenian Revenue committee for one study visit to Sweden in order to outline the possible cooperation areas where the STA can contribute to strengthening the SRC with a focus on capacity building and exchange of experiences. The point of departure for any support and cooperation is to be Swedens strategy for reform cooperation in Eastern Europe.
The objectives of the fact-finding phase are:
1. To establish contact with key staff and management at the SRC and other relevant stakeholders such as the Embassy of Sweden, IMF, EU, World Bank and other donors of importance for designing the possible future support.
2.To collect information from the SRC about the tax system in Armenia as well as the context where the authority is operating. Elaborating a strategic analysis of the current situation and needs is also envisaged. Issues relating the so-called crosscutting perspectives (i.e. gender equality, poverty, HRBA, environment and climate change and conflict) will also be addressed, with special attention to matters on gender equality and taxation as well as womens participation in the labour market.
3. Identify areas of possible Swedish support where Sweden has knowledge and a special nisch.
4. To prepare a draft project document that includes potential areas of cooperation and the future modalities of the cooperation as well as resultatsmatrix and wider analysis of the system that the the Armenian State Revenue Committee, SRC, is part of.
5. The TADAT-assessment managed by IMF with support from STA, mentioned in the budget, will enhance the context analysis for the project proposal and inform the selection of priorities. The Tax administration Diagnostic Assessment Tool (TADAT) is designed to provide an objective assessment of the health of key components of a countrys system of tax administration. This framework is focused on the nine key performance outcome areas (POAs) that cover most tax administration functions, processes and institutions. The assessment of these performance outcome areas is based on 32 high-level indicators that are each built on 1 to 5 dimensions that together add up to 55 measurement dimensions, making TADAT a comprehensive but administrable diagnostic tool.
As noted above, the IMF has expressed interest in having STA-experts on-board for the TADAT-assessment, which is scheduled for 12 May 2025. The STA believes it would be very beneficial for a potential cooperation project, if they could take part in the assessment in order to gather facts and establishing working relations with the future partner. Consequently, the fact-finding proposal and budget also includes a request for funding for the STAs participation in the TADAT-assessment, which is approved by Sida.
